claims.claim: In-batch negatives are a training strategy for DPR.
Negative passages are taken from other questions in the same mini-batch.
For a mini-batch of size B, each question has a relevant passage.
The model computes a similarity matrix S of size B x B.
Each row of the similarity matrix corresponds to a question.
Each column of the similarity matrix corresponds to a passage.
Pairs (qi, pj) with i != j are treated as negative examples.
The diagonal pair (qi, pi) is the positive example.
Each batch yields B(B-1) negative pairs.
This approach reuses passages already present in the batch.
It effectively increases the number of training examples.
It provides a memory-efficient way to generate negatives.
DPR main experiments use in-batch negatives with batch size 128.
DPR main experiments use one additional BM25 negative per question.
